A full-page illustration plate from a 19th-century adventure book about the sea. Technique: a copper-plate engraving with etching, printed in a single dark sepia-brown ink on plain white paper. The tone values come only from the thickness and spacing of the lines: no grey wash, no aquatint, no tonal gradients, no airbrush, no smudged pencil shading, no colour; between the lines the paper stays white. The sky is ruled with long, perfectly even horizontal lines, close together and thick at the top of the sky, thinning out towards a light band at the horizon; the low clouds are shaped only by thicker and thinner ruling and a few contour lines. The calm sea is drawn with long horizontal, slightly wavy lines with white gaps for the reflections. Nocturne mood with strong contrast: deep cross-hatched darks in the cottage, the rocks and the boat hulls; bare white paper only at the lights, the horizon band and the reflections. The lines must be crisp, clearly separated and bold enough to stay readable when the picture is shown at screen size: about 200 lines across the height of the picture in the sky and the water, never a dense grey mush. Not a photograph, not a 3D render, not a painting, not a pencil drawing, not a woodcut, not a cartoon, not a postcard. No aged paper texture, no stains, no frame, no border line, no plate mark, no caption.
